concepts.why: Secular scholar / Jewish reader of the Hebrew Bible: the name says the blood is the life, and Genesis 9:4, Leviticus 17:11 and 17:14 and Deuteronomy 12:23 say so; Hebrews 9:22 says that without blood there is no forgiveness and says nothing about life. It shares the word blood without holding the concept. Move it to 'To make atonement' (n 13), where Hebrews already sits beside the Levitical priests.

concepts.name: Fire consumed the sacrifice
concepts.why: Secular scholar: 'came down from heaven' is said only by 1 Chronicles 21:26 ('fire from heaven') and 2 Chronicles 7:1 ('came down from heaven'). Leviticus 9:24 has fire 'out from the presence of the LORD', Judges 6:21 has fire that 'flared from the rock', and 1 Kings 18:38 has the fire 'fell'. The name says more than three of the five passages. 'Fire consumed the sacrifice' is in Leviticus 9:24, Judges 6:21, 1 Kings 18:38 and 2 Chronicles 7:1 in the texts' own words; 1 Chronicles 21:26 says the LORD answered with fire on the altar of burnt offering, which the same plain label covers.

Secular scholar / Reformed: the name says the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit, which only Psalm 51:17 says; Psalm 51:19 follows it without saying it, and Isaiah 66:2-3 does not say it at all (verse 2 esteems the humble; verse 3 compares sacrifice to killing a man, which cuts against the name). Isaiah 66:3 is already under 'I will not accept them' (n 24), so the verse stands twice under opposite headings. Drop the passage here. If a second witness to the contrite spirit is wanted, give Isaiah 66:2 alone, but then the name should become 'A broken and a contrite heart' (Psalm 51:17's words) and Psalm 51:19 should stay only in the secondary 'Sacrifices of righteousness' row.

concepts.name: They sacrificed their sons and their daughters
concepts.why: Secular scholar: 'in the fire' is in Deuteronomy 12:31, 2 Kings 16:3, 17:17, Jeremiah 7:31 and Ezekiel 16:21 but not in Leviticus 18:21 (Molech) or Psalm 106:37-38 (demons, idols of Canaan). The name says more than two passages. Psalm 106:37 and 2 Kings 17:17 give a plain name in the texts' words that all seven hold.

Secular scholar / biblical-theological reader: Romans 6:10 shares the words 'once for all' but speaks of dying to sin and living to God, not of an offering or a sacrifice; every other passage here (Hebrews 7:27, 9:12, 9:25-28, 10:10-14, 1 Peter 3:18) is about the one offering for sins. It does not hold the concept under this theme. (Hebrews 9:25-28 and 10:10-14 run on into the second appearing and the footstool of the enemies; they are the texts' own words and I leave them, but a reader of the last things will notice them here.)

Secular scholar: the name is 'he will be forgiven', and Hebrews 10:19-22 says to draw near with hearts sprinkled; it does not say forgiven, and Hebrews 10:22 is already under 'Sprinkled and made clean' (n 16). It is longer than the concept needs. With it dropped the last concept ends on Hebrews 10:17-18 (sins remembered no more; where forgiven, an offering for sin is no longer needed), which carries the hope in the texts' own words. Nothing dark is softened: 'I will not accept them' (n 24) and 'Sons and daughters' (n 26) still stand. 1 John 1:7 says 'cleanses' rather than 'forgiven' but is kept as the New Testament's matching word; acceptable.

secondary_or_links: The mercy seat -> I will meet with you there: the label is Exodus 25:22's; Leviticus 16:2 says the LORD appears in the cloud above the mercy seat and Hebrews 9:5 says only 'overshadowing the mercy seat'. Either name the row 'The mercy seat' with no arrow, or keep the arrow and accept that two of three passages do not carry the phrase (secular scholar: name says more than its passages).

Sacrificed to demons -> not to God: Leviticus 17:7 ('goat demons') and Psalm 106:37 do not say 'not to God'; Deuteronomy 32:17 and 1 Corinthians 10:20 do. Acceptable as a row label taken from the Deuteronomy text; no change needed.

Order of the last three concepts: 'Accepted on My altar' (n 31, including Jeremiah 33:18 that the Levites will never fail to offer burnt offerings) sits directly before 'And he will be forgiven' (ending on Hebrews 10:17-18, 'an offering for sin is no longer needed'). The pair is left unharmonised, which is right; no note or heading may be added between them that reconciles them (Reformed, Lutheran, dispensational and Catholic readers all read these two differently).

Isaiah 53 beside Acts 8:32-33 (n 25): acceptable. Acts quotes the Isaiah passage in its own words, Jeremiah 11:19 shows the same image used of the prophet himself, and no note says one is about the other. Do not add a line to the card or note that does.

Hebrews beside the Levitical texts in 'Without blemish', 'Outside the camp', 'Sprinkled and made clean', 'The Passover lamb' and 'Once for all': each names only a shared phrase and each New Testament passage draws its own comparison in its own words; none of the concept names says fulfilled or points to. Acceptable as it stands.
Link Messiah/Christology: acceptable as a theme link to shared passages; add no card text beside it.

missing.why: Plainly and widely developed: it is the first of the offerings of Leviticus and the one named most across the books (Genesis 8:20; 22:2; Exodus 29:18; Judges 11:31; 1 Kings 18:38; Psalm 51:19), but it has no concept of its own; it appears only inside 'A pleasing aroma', 'Abraham offered Isaac' and a secondary row on the regular burnt offering. A reader of Leviticus 1-7 will expect the burnt offering to be named beside the peace, sin and guilt offerings. Name it in Leviticus 1's words (the whole animal burned on the altar), without adding a gloss.
